significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that, for some established cause→effect pairs, “steering the cause direction should shift the model's prediction of the effect more than” the reverse and the cause subspace should predict the effect better than vice versa; this is a form-(iii) ordering and predictive coupling between measurable intervention effects. It would establish a representational phenomenon plus bounded mechanistic evidence, fixing the expected sign of forward-versus-reverse interventions and bearing directly on the intervention-respecting correspondence emphasized in Schölkopf et al.'s 2021 causal-representation-learning agenda, although it would not establish the model's complete scientific mechanism. The negative branch would meaningfully reject this proposed asymmetry as a general diagnostic of mechanistic encoding, but the wording “present for some scientific relationships and absent for others” weakens determinacy at the aggregate level and a null would not exclude nonlinear or distributed causal representations. Topic substitution does not preserve the score: merely asking whether scientific mechanisms are represented would merit the topic median, whereas the directional intervention ordering is a sharper, claim-specific constraint.

reach.justification: The named handles are the “Causal-Asymmetry Score,” an “open directed-mechanism benchmark,” and a “per-model Causal-Asymmetry leaderboard,” which could support comparative model auditing. These are principally post-hoc diagnostics of a representation already learned rather than forecasts of a downstream scientific failure, though an auditor could use them before deciding whether to rely on a model. After re-extraction on another model, the claim does not predict which relationships will exhibit asymmetry—it explicitly allows asymmetry to be “present for some scientific relationships and absent for others”—so mainly the measurement procedure transfers, despite the asserted cross-domain scope and possible uptake by scientific-model auditors. Topic substitution would not retain this reach score because the reusable CAS audit is specific to the claim, but its pair- and model-specific conclusions keep it near the topic's default diagnostic reach.
